saml.description: Vault SAML auth does not validate response or assertion signatures unless validate_response_signature and/or validate_assertion_signature are explicitly enabled.
saml.note: Acceptance of attacker-signed or unsigned SAML material under default config is an insecure default/hardening issue, not evidence that Vault ignored explicitly enabled validation.

saml.description: A valid unexpired Vault bearer token can be reused across multiple API calls until TTL or num_uses limits are reached.
saml.note: Do not flag ordinary reuse of the same Vault token as replay unless a one-time or limited-use setting was explicitly configured.

saml.description: Token self-lookup is a normal authenticated API call and counts against token_num_uses when that limit is configured.
saml.note: A later secret read failing after lookup-self on a low-use token is expected budget exhaustion, not necessarily an authorization bug.

saml.description: Vault token use budget of 0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses.
saml.source: Vault token auth API documentation for num_uses/token_num_uses
saml.note: Prevents false positives in replay and freshness tests.

saml.description: When group_policy_application_mode is set to any, identity group policies apply regardless of namespace hierarchy.
saml.note: Cross-namespace policy reach in this mode is by design and should not be flagged as escalation without showing it exceeds configured admin intent.

saml.description: Admin changes to SAML IdP metadata URL, certificate, or entity ID immediately redefine the trusted upstream IdP for future logins.
saml.note: A login succeeding after an admin reconfigured the SAML trust anchor is authorized behavior, not trust-anchor substitution by an attacker.

saml.description: Admin changes to SAML config, role constraints, or trust settings take effect for subsequent logins by design.
saml.source: Vault SAML auth API docs: config and role update endpoints
saml.note: A login succeeding because an admin changed trust anchors or role settings is expected behavior, not a trust-anchor substitution attack.

saml.description: Vault token self-lookup display_name may include auth mount metadata as a prefix before the user identity.
saml.source: Vault token lookup-self sample response shows prefixed display_name pattern such as ldap2-tesla
saml.note: Do not treat mount-prefixed display_name values as identity collisions if the suffix matches the sent identity.

saml.constraint: SAML signature validation is opt-in in Vault SAML auth config: validate_response_signature defaults to false and validate_assertion_signature defaults to false. For I1 saml_cert_substitution and unsigned/spurious-signature tests, the fuzzer MUST explicitly control these flags. To test insecure defaults, leave both unset/false; to test hardened behavior, set both true. Do not assume signatures are validated unless these options are enabled.

Issuer validation depends on IdP configuration. If idp_metadata_url is used, issuer/trust comes from metadata. If manual config is used, idp_entity_id is required alongside idp_sso_url and idp_cert. For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, the fuzzer MUST configure either metadata with the intended trusted issuer or manual idp_entity_id explicitly; otherwise issuer-validation behavior may be skipped or misconfigured.

SAML ACS URL used in the login flow must exactly match one of the configured acs_urls. The sso_service_url endpoint requires acs_url and states it must be in the configured set. For all SAML tests, the fuzzer MUST use an acs_url already present in config or the flow will fail for setup reasons unrelated to the invariant under test.

Vault SAML login is a 3-step flow bound by token_poll_id and PKCE-like challenge values: first obtain /sso_service_url with client_challenge, then POST SAMLResponse to /callback, then exchange token_poll_id plus matching client_verifier at /token. For I3 flow-coherence tests, the fuzzer MUST preserve this binding across the same flow and MUST NOT mix token_poll_id or verifier values across sessions unless intentionally testing session confusion.
saml.source: auth/saml.mdx obtain SSO service URL, callback, obtain vault token

saml.constraint: bound_subjects matching is controlled by bound_subjects_type. If bound_subjects_type=string, matching is exact string only; if glob, * wildcards are supported. For I4 multi-identity tests, if multiple different subjects must pass the same role, the fuzzer MUST either omit bound_subjects entirely or set bound_subjects_type=glob with an intentional pattern. Do NOT set bound_subjects='*' without bound_subjects_type=glob; in string mode it matches only the literal '*'.

bound_attributes matching is controlled by bound_attributes_type, which defaults to string. In string mode, attribute values require exact string match; in glob mode, * wildcards are supported. For I4/I5 multi-identity tests, exact-match attribute constraints MUST be omitted if different values need to authenticate through the same role. Do NOT use wildcard-looking values under the default string mode because they are treated literally.

bound_attributes accepts expected values as a single string or comma-separated list of strings, and authentication succeeds if the SAML attributes match at least one expected value. For I5 tests, this is string-list membership semantics, not numeric/boolean typed comparison. The fuzzer SHOULD treat these as string comparisons only and avoid assuming native numeric coercion behavior is documented.

token_num_uses limits total uses of the issued Vault token, and value 0 is a sentinel meaning unlimited uses, not literal zero. Every API call made with the session token consumes a use budget, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the fuzzer performs both verification and resource access, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3+ if additional session-inspection calls are included.
saml.source: auth/saml.mdx read role; tokenfields via role config

saml.constraint: Vault token and KV v2 numeric sentinels must be handled precisely. token_num_uses=0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. KV v2 engine config max_versions=0 means keep the platform default of 10 versions, not zero versions. KV v2 delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic timed deletion, not immediate deletion. Never interpret these sentinel values as literal zero behavior.
saml.source: auth/saml.mdx read role; secret/kv/kv-v2.mdx configure KV engine

saml.constraint: For I2 SAML replay and expiry tests, include a control login through the same configured flow before the attack login. Without a successful control using the same role/config, a failed replay or expired-assertion attempt cannot be distinguished from broken SAML setup, ACS mismatch, or token_poll/verifier mismatch.

Vault token lookup-self returns ttl, creation_ttl, expire_time, and num_uses for the current token. For freshness tests, the fuzzer SHOULD use lookup-self as the authoritative source for post-login token lifetime/usage state rather than inferring from role config alone, because issued token values may reflect defaults or mount/system tuning.

KV v2 protected-resource reads must use the /data/ path segment. Reading /v1/{engine}/data/{path} is required for actual secret access tests; using the mount root or KV v1-style path will produce false 404/permission results unrelated to authorization.

KV v2 listing uses /metadata/ paths and requires list capability there even if reads use /data/. For authorization tests, the fuzzer MUST not treat inability to LIST /metadata/ as evidence that READ /data/ is denied, or vice versa; these are distinct capabilities and paths.

External identity groups used for SAML group aliasing should be modeled with aliases rather than manual member_entity_ids when testing external group mapping. The SAML role's groups_attribute creates identity group aliases from assertion group names, so the fuzzer SHOULD create identity groups and group aliases tied to the SAML mount accessor instead of trying to simulate external membership by directly editing entity membership.

MFA login enforcement creation requires at least one target selector among auth_method_accessors, auth_method_types, identity_group_ids, or identity_entity_ids. For I3 saml_mfa_bypass_via_binding_rule tests, the fuzzer MUST scope the enforcement to the SAML auth mount accessor or auth method type; creating an enforcement with only mfa_method_ids is invalid setup.

Group policy application mode affects whether identity group policies apply only within namespace hierarchy or across any namespace. The default is within_namespace_hierarchy; mode any broadens policy application across namespaces. For I5 group-policy escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST record and control /sys/config/group-policy-application because cross-namespace group policy effects may be by design under mode=any.

Issuer binding is only enforced when the auth method is configured with idp_entity_id (or via trusted metadata). For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch default-config tests, if idp_metadata_url is used or idp_entity_id is omitted in manual config, issuer validation behavior may differ or be skipped. The fuzzer must intentionally choose manual config without idp_entity_id when testing skipped issuer validation, and set idp_entity_id when testing issuer enforcement.

The SAML ACS/login flow is multi-step and session-bound: obtain SSO service URL returns token_poll_id and requires a client_challenge derived from the later client_verifier; the callback completes validation; the token endpoint requires the matching client_verifier and token_poll_id. For I3 flow-coherence tests, reuse the same flow artifacts within one login attempt and do not mix token_poll_id/client_verifier across flows.

SAML login in Vault is not a single POST-to-token endpoint. A valid test flow must initiate the SAML flow first so the SP issues RelayState/AuthnRequest context, then submit the SAMLResponse to /auth/{mount}/callback, then exchange at /auth/{mount}/token. Sending a fabricated callback without SP-initiated flow context will fail for protocol reasons, not security reasons.

Role matching semantics: bound_subjects supports two modes controlled by bound_subjects_type. If bound_subjects_type=string, matching is exact string only. If bound_subjects_type=glob, '*' wildcard matching is enabled. For I4 multi-identity tests, do not set bound_subjects='*' unless bound_subjects_type=glob; with string mode it matches only the literal '*'.

Attribute matching semantics: bound_attributes matching mode is controlled by bound_attributes_type. Default is string, which requires direct string match; glob enables wildcard matching. For I4 multi-identity tests that need multiple distinct attribute values to pass the same role, omit the exact-match attribute constraint or switch to glob intentionally. Do not assume wildcards work in default string mode.

bound_attributes values are documented as single strings or comma-separated lists of strings. For I5 claim/attribute type-coercion tests, Vault SAML role constraints are string-oriented; non-string SAML attribute typing is not documented here. The fuzzer should treat bound_attributes as string matching only and avoid interpreting numeric/boolean coercion results as supported behavior without explicit evidence.

token_num_uses is a use-budget limiter on issued Vault tokens. Value 0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. Every API call made with that session token consumes a use, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the sequence performs both self-lookup and secret-read verification, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3+ if any additional session-authenticated call is included.
Vault token numeric sentinel: token_num_uses=0 means unlimited uses. Do not interpret 0 as 'deny all' or 'single use disabled by zero'. This affects I2 replay/use-budget tests and cleanup sequencing.

Vault token TTL sentinel behavior appears in role reads as token_ttl=0, token_max_ttl=0, token_explicit_max_ttl=0, token_period=0. In Vault token fields, 0 means use system/mount defaults or no explicit override, not literal immediate expiry. Never assume 0 disables the underlying token or makes it instantly expired.

KV v2 pathing is mandatory for secret verification and seeding. For verify_read_secret and seed_protected_resource on versioned KV mounts, the path must include /data/. Using /v1/{engine}/{path} instead of /v1/{engine}/data/{path} will hit the wrong API shape and produce false failures.

Vault group aliasing for SAML groups requires the auth mount accessor. To map SAML groups_attribute values into identity groups, create an external identity group and then create a group alias with mount_accessor for the SAML auth mount. Do not try to attach external group membership directly via member_entity_ids for this purpose.

Identity group policy application can vary globally by /sys/config/group-policy-application. Default mode within_namespace_hierarchy restricts when group policies apply across namespaces; mode any relaxes this. For I5 group-policy escalation tests, account for this global mode or cross-namespace results may be by design rather than a broker authorization bug.

For I2 SAML freshness tests such as expired assertions, include a control login through the same configured SAML flow first. Without a successful control, a failed expired-assertion attempt cannot be distinguished from broken SAML setup, bad ACS URL, or mismatched flow artifacts.

Vault SAML config accepts either idp_metadata_url or the manual trio idp_sso_url + idp_entity_id + idp_cert. These are mutually exclusive. The fuzzer must not send metadata URL together with manual trust-anchor fields in the same config update, or setup will be invalid for reasons unrelated to the invariant under test.

SAML signature validation is opt-in in Vault SAML config: validate_response_signature defaults to false and validate_assertion_signature defaults to false. For I1 signature-integrity tests, the fuzzer MUST explicitly set these booleans according to the test objective. To test insecure defaults, leave them unset/false; to test enforcement, enable the relevant flag(s).

Issuer validation depends on configured IdP trust. If idp_metadata_url is used, Vault derives IdP metadata including issuer/cert from metadata. If manual config is used, idp_entity_id and idp_cert are required together with idp_sso_url. For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, the fuzzer MUST configure a trusted IdP entity ID and then send a different assertion Issuer; omitting idp_entity_id in manual mode is invalid setup, while relying on metadata means issuer comes from metadata.

bound_subjects matching semantics are controlled by bound_subjects_type. If bound_subjects_type=string, matching is exact string only; if bound_subjects_type=glob, '*' wildcard matching is enabled. For I4 multi-identity tests, the fuzzer MUST NOT set bound_subjects='*' unless bound_subjects_type=glob. If multiple different subjects must authenticate through the same role under exact-match semantics, bound_subjects MUST be omitted entirely.

bound_attributes matching semantics are controlled by bound_attributes_type, which defaults to string. In string mode, attribute values are exact string matches; in glob mode, '*' wildcard matching is enabled. For I4/I5 tests requiring multiple different attribute values to pass the same role, the fuzzer MUST either set bound_attributes_type=glob with explicit wildcard intent or omit the constraint. Do NOT assume '*' works under the default string mode.

bound_attributes values are documented as single strings or comma-separated lists of strings. Vault authenticates if SAML attributes match at least one expected value. For I5 claim/attribute type-coercion tests, non-string SAML attribute typing is not documented; the fuzzer SHOULD treat bound_attributes as string-valued matching only and avoid interpreting acceptance/rejection of non-string encodings as a definitive bug without a string-valued control.

token_num_uses limits every API call made with the issued Vault token, including verify_granted_identity via /auth/token/lookup-self and verify_read_secret. Minimum safe value is 2 if the sequence performs both self-lookup and secret-read after login; use 3+ if any additional session-authenticated verification calls are inserted. token_num_uses=0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses.

Numeric sentinel semantics for token_num_uses: value 0 means unlimited uses, not literal zero. Never configure token_num_uses=0 when intending a one-time token test; use 1 for single-use behavior and remember that pre-access verification calls consume that single use.

Numeric sentinel semantics for KV v2 max_versions: value 0 or unset does not mean keep zero versions; it means Vault keeps the default 10 versions. Do not use max_versions=0 in tests expecting immediate version eviction.
Numeric sentinel semantics for KV v2 delete_version_after: value '0s' means no automatic deletion timer, not immediate deletion. Do not interpret '0s' as delete instantly.

For I2 SAML replay tests, a valid control flow is required because Vault SAML login is multi-step: obtain SSO service URL, complete ACS callback, then exchange token_poll_id plus client_verifier at /auth/{mount}/token. A failed final token exchange can reflect broken flow state rather than replay protection. The fuzzer MUST compare against a control login using the same setup but without the replay mutation.

For I2 saml_assertion_id_replay and saml_one_time_use_replay tests, the replayed assertion must be submitted through the same documented SAML flow shape so that Vault actually consumes the repeated assertion. Replaying only the final /auth/{mount}/token exchange tests token_poll_id/client_verifier flow state, not SAML assertion replay handling.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion tests, include a control login with a non-expired assertion first. Without a control, rejection of the expired assertion cannot be distinguished from broken SAML flow setup or mismatched RelayState/InResponseTo handling.

Vault SAML callback requires RelayState from the original SP-initiated flow. The executor MUST initiate the SAML flow first and preserve the returned RelayState/flow state before posting SAMLResponse to /auth/{mount}/callback. Fabricated standalone callback posts without matching flow state will be rejected for flow reasons, causing false positives in I1/I2/I3 tests.

For I3 config-change tests, changes to /auth/{mount}/config or /auth/{mount}/role/{role_name} are expected to affect subsequent new logins immediately. Do NOT flag a login succeeding or failing under the new admin-authorized configuration as a coherence bug by itself; the test must show stale evaluation against the old config after the change.

groups_attribute controls which SAML attribute names are used to create Identity group aliases on successful login. For I5 group-policy-escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST pre-create matching identity groups and group aliases using the SAML mount accessor; otherwise missing alias mappings can make group-derived policy behavior appear absent for setup reasons rather than enforcement reasons.

Vault KV v2 secret reads use /v1/{engine}/data/{path}, while list operations use /metadata/. For verify_read_secret, the fuzzer MUST use the /data/ path. Using the mount root or KV v1 path shape will produce 404/permission errors unrelated to authorization.
